steps.tx: Surgical abdominoplasty restores contour by addressing the structural triad of lower abdominal skin redundancy, subcutaneous adipose excess, and **rectus abdominis diastasis**. Patient selection carefully evaluates whether tissue laxity is predominantly supraumbilical, infraumbilical, or circumferential following massive bariatric weight loss and pregnancy changes.
steps.say: Surgeons identify that surgeons identify that abdominoplasty corrects abdominal skin redundancy, excess subcutaneous fat, and rectus muscle diastasis. Evaluation determines if laxity is localized or circumferential after weight loss.

nodes.label: Structural evaluation: skin excess, fat distribution, fascial laxity
Incision planning and selective epigastric tunnel undermining
Two-layer rectus plication, quilting sutures, and umbilical inset

steps.tx: In full abdominoplasty, the abdominal flap is elevated off the rectus sheath up to the costal margins, while preserving lateral blood supply. Midline **rectus diastasis plication** is executed using two layers of interrupted and continuous permanent monofilament or braided sutures to re-establish an athletic abdominal wall profile.
steps.say: During full abdominoplasty, the abdominal flap is elevated to the costal margins. Surgeons identify that a two-layer plication reapproximates the separated rectus abdominis muscles in the midline.

steps.tx: Surgical variants depend on tissue laxity distribution. **Mini-abdominoplasty** involves limited infraumbilical skin excision and infraumbilical plication without transposing the umbilicus. **Fleur-de-lis abdominoplasty** combines standard low transverse excision with a vertical midline resection, ideal for massive weight loss patients with pronounced horizontal skin excess.
steps.say: Surgeons identify that variants include mini-abdominoplasty for isolated lower laxity without umbilical relocation, and Fleur-de-lis abdominoplasty with vertical resection for massive horizontal laxity.

steps.tx: In high-superior tension abdominoplasty described by Lockwood, substantial closure tension is transferred to the **superficial fascial system** or SFS anchored firmly to the deep iliac fascia. This mechanical suspension prevents cranial scar migration, maintains low suprapubic scar placement, and avoids mons pubis elevation.
steps.say: Surgeons identify that surgeons identify that lockwood high-superior tension abdominoplasty anchors the superficial fascial system to deep iliac fascia. Surgeons identify that this maintains a low suprapubic scar and avoids upward scar migration.

nodes.label: Flap advancement under high superior traction
Deep suture anchoring of SFS to iliac fascia

steps.tx: Baroudi and Ferreira introduced **progressive tension sutures** (quilting sutures) placed between the advancing abdominal flap and the underlying rectus fascia. These interrupted absorbable sutures incrementally advance the flap downward, completely obliterate subcutaneous dead space, and reduce seroma formation rates to under 2%.
steps.say: Surgeons identify that progressive tension quilting sutures anchor the abdominal flap to the rectus fascia. Surgeons identify that obliterating dead space eliminates seroma formation and avoids surgical drains.

steps.tx: A **circumferential body lift** or belt lipectomy extends the low transverse excision 360 degrees around the torso, indicated for massive weight loss patients. It synchronizes abdominoplasty with lateral thigh lifting and gluteal suspension, performed in prone and supine stages during a single operative session.
steps.say: Surgeons identify that surgeons identify that a circumferential body lift extends the excision 360 degrees around the waist. Surgeons identify that surgeons identify that it simultaneously corrects abdominal, lateral thigh, and gluteal laxity in massive weight loss patients.

rows: Lower back excision, buttock elevation and suspension
Abdominoplasty, rectus plication, and mons reduction

steps.tx: Deep venous thrombosis and **pulmonary embolism** are the leading causes of mortality in major abdominoplasty procedures. Routine prophylactic protocols mandate Caprini score assessment, intraoperative pneumatic calf compression devices, early aggressive ambulation, and chemical thromboprophylaxis with low-molecular-weight heparin in high-risk patients.
steps.say: Venous thromboembolism is the leading cause of mortality following abdominoplasty. Risk assessment with Caprini scores, compression boots, and low-molecular-weight heparin is mandatory.

steps.tx: Skin flap necrosis occurs predominantly in the central supra-incisional region, corresponding to Huger Zone I. Risk factors include wide lateral subflap undermining dividing intercostal perforators, concurrent aggressive liposuction, smoking, and prior scars such as subcostal Kocher incisions compromising collateral **perforator circulation**.
steps.say: Surgeons identify that surgeons identify that flap necrosis most commonly occurs centrally in Huger Zone one. Surgeons identify that excessive lateral undermining, cigarette smoking, and prior abdominal scars increase ischemic risk.
